Report_ID: Participants with one or more adverse experiences (any type) within 42 days after vaccination
Title: Efficacy and safety of live varicella zoster vaccine in diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Hata et al.
Comment: Both arms also received concurrent PPSV23, so adverse events reflect the combination in both arms (schedule is identical across arms). Vaccine is the BIKEN Oka varicella vaccine (~50,000 pfu), which the authors designate 'varicella zoster vaccine' and argue is equivalent to Zostavax. P-value is from the paper's chi-square test; no risk ratio was reported by the paper.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Live attenuated Oka varicella zoster vaccine (+ concurrent PPSV23)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Recruitment source: Kitano Hospital, a general hospital in Osaka, Japan
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of participants presenting at least one adverse experience, ITT set
Outcome variable: Participants with one or more adverse experiences (any type) within 42 days after vaccination
outcome_family: one or more adverse events (any adverse event)
effect_direction: RR < 1 (5/27 = 18.5% with vaccine vs 6/27 = 22.2% with placebo; slightly fewer participants with any AE in vaccine arm, not significant)

Report_ID: Subjects with one or more adverse experience (AE), days 1-28 post-vaccination
Title: Safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity of zoster vaccine in subjects with a history of herpes zoster
Author: Mills et al.
Comment: Denominators used are the numbers of subjects per vaccination group as given in Table 2 (100 vaccine, 101 placebo) per the synthesis plan; the paper's own percentages (52.0%, 17.7%) are calculated on subjects with follow-up (98 and 96). Crossover design, so arms are not independent; no significance test reported for this outcome (estimation study).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('ZOSTAVAX (zoster vaccine live, single 0.65-mL SC dose)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults >=50 years of age with physician-documented history of herpes zoster >=5 years prior to study entry
Recruitment source: 9 US study sites (ZOSTAVAX Protocol 014, NCT00322231), May 2006 - July 2007
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of subjects with one or more AE of any type (injection-site or systemic, vaccine-related or not) within 28 days post-vaccination
Outcome variable: Subjects with one or more adverse experience (AE), days 1-28 post-vaccination
outcome_family: one or more adverse events (any adverse event)
effect_direction: RR > 1 (51/100 with Zostavax vs 17/101 with placebo; more participants with any AE after vaccine)

Report_ID: Subjects with one or more adverse experiences (any AE), Days 0–42 postvaccination 1
Title: Safety, tolerability, and immunogenicity after 1 and 2 doses of zoster vaccine in healthy adults ≥60 years of age
Author: Vermeulen et al.
Comment: Paper reports no p-value or risk ratio for the 'one or more AE' outcome; only counts and percentages. One randomised subject in the ZV arm was not vaccinated and was excluded, so the vaccinated denominator is 104 (210 randomised).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Zoster vaccine (ZV, ~23,000 PFU/0.5 mL, dose 1)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Healthy adults ≥60 years of age with a history of varicella and no prior herpes zoster
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of subjects with one or more AE
Outcome variable: Subjects with one or more adverse experiences (any AE), Days 0–42 postvaccination 1
outcome_family: one or more adverse events (any adverse event)
effect_direction: RR > 1 (74/104 = 71.2% with zoster vaccine vs 46/105 = 43.8% with placebo; more participants with any AE after vaccine)

Report_ID: One or more adverse events (any type), day of vaccination to day 42
Title: A Vaccine to Prevent Herpes Zoster and Postherpetic Neuralgia in Older Adults
Author: Oxman MN, et al. (Shingles Prevention Study Group)
Comment: P value recorded as the reported threshold P<0.05 (exact value not given). Reported effect measure is a difference in risk (23.7%, 95% CI 21.3-26.0), not a ratio; table percentages are age-weighted rates among subjects with safety follow-up, so 58.1% and 34.4% do not exactly equal 1929/3345 and 1117/3271.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Zoster vaccine (live attenuated Oka/Merck VZV vaccine, single 0.5 ml SC injection)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Immunocompetent adults 60 years of age or older with history of varicella or >=30 years residence in continental USA
Recruitment source: 22 clinical study sites (mostly VA medical centers and academic centers), November 1998 - September 2001
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of substudy subjects with >=1 adverse event of any type during days 0-42 after vaccination
Outcome variable: One or more adverse events (any type), day of vaccination to day 42
outcome_family: one or more adverse events (any adverse event)
effect_direction: RR > 1 (1929/3345 with vaccine vs 1117/3271 with placebo; significantly more participants with any AE after vaccine, risk difference 23.7%)
